subject: Min and max values for semTools' plotProbe

messages.author: c676d94b8ba27cbe
messages.subject: Min and max values for semTools' plotProbe
parts:
Hello all - 
Maybe this is easier than I am making it out to be, but I have an interaction between a latent variable and an observed variable predicting a latent variable outcome.  I would like to chart the interaction to visually show the relationship and am using the probe2WayMC and plotProbe functions from semTools to do so.  The moderating values used in probe2WayMC function are from the observed variable, but how do I know likely min/max values of the exogenous latent variable for the "xlim= " in the plotProbe function?  

Thanks for any help/hints!  Cheers,
Aaron

messages.author: 5d4f9e7f97c21008
messages.subject: Re: Min and max values for semTools' plotProbe
parts:
Hi Aaron,

I would look at the mean and variance of the latent variable and plot from -2SD to +2SD based on those values. Depending on how you set the scale of the latent variable these values might differ (e.g. if you set the variance of the latent to 1.0, and the mean to 0, the range would be -2, to 2). However you could pick other values as well. The xlim option simply sets the range of values on the x axis, so any "reasonable" values would work well.

Alex

Thanks for this.  To be clear on this, the "std.lv=TRUE" argument should set the scale of the latent variable to variance=1/mean=0, right?  The reason I ask is because when I set xlim to (-2,2) I get slopes that don't make as much sense.  Below zero (x-axis), I get lower values for the slope lines that should be higher (which they are above 0).  (see attached examples, Rplot2 is the one that makes more sense)

Also, how would I go about figuring out "reasonable" values for xlim?  The chart makes more sense with xlim set to something like (0,4), but I obviously want a correct representation of the relationships.  Is there a way to get a sense of the latent variable's min and max?  I am predicting mental health, so negative values don't really make sense, but I am unsure how to figure something like that out.  inspect(sem.object, "mean.lv") gives me a sense of the LV mean at least, right?

Thanks again Alex (and anyone else!). 

Cheers,
Aaron

messages.author: 5d4f9e7f97c21008
messages.subject: Re: Min and max values for semTools' plotProbe
parts:
If you're using std.lv=TRUE then the latent variables have means of 0 and variances (or residual variances) of 1.0. This is the key to all of your questions. It means that both the IV and the DV have means of 0 (the IV has a variance of 1.0, the DV has a residual variance of 1.0). So, having negative values of the DV makes perfect sense (it just means that the scores are below the mean). If you want to keep your variables in their original metric, I would recommend using effects coding as your method of scale setting.

In terms of what is "reasonable" in this situation, that's up to you. I would add that plotting from 0-4 on the X axis doesn't make a lot of sense (you're only plotting values of X that are above the mean of X, which strikes me as odd).

Alex
